clue.text: Orchestral instrument from my supermarket

parts.note: 'cor' is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'
Netto is a discount supermarket chain

explanation.surface: A musician buys an instrument at the local discount shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' is the exclamation, not a possessive. COR is British slang for surprise; Netto is a Danish discount grocery chain that once traded in the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: The cornetto is a Renaissance wind instrument, a wooden horn with fingerholes, still heard in early-music orchestras.

clue.text: Avant-garde piece from talented gypsy

indicators.note: piece from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A gifted traveller plays a daring, experimental piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cutting-edge and experimental is described informally as being at the edge, unconventional and daring.

clue.text: Country song oddly about drug: moving ecstasy

indicators.note: moving says one letter is shifted to a new place in the word
about means the odd letters go around the word for the drug
oddly keeps the first and third letters of the word song

parts.note: weed is slang for cannabis
E is the abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A national song about drugs gets people dancing on ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country song' suggests country music, but 'Country' alone is the definition; 'moving' shifts one of the two E's along a place.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scandinavian nation, a country bordering Norway and Finland.

clue.text: E.g. a little Calypso number turned up, keeping variable speed

indicators.note: keeping means the reversed number holds the other letters inside it
turned up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: ten is a number
Y is a standard algebraic variable
mph, miles per hour, measures speed

explanation.surface: A calypso song played with a varying tempo.
explanation.walkthrough: Calypso here is the sea nymph of the Odyssey, not the Caribbean song; 'turned up' makes NET, and 'keeping' puts Y and MPH inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A young nymph is a diminutive one, so a small version of a sea goddess like Calypso fits the term.

clue.text: Nothing in set due to change with ten DJs

indicators.note: to change says the letters of set due, together with the zero and the ten, are rearranged

parts.note: O is the figure zero, nothing
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Disc jockeys are booked to change over with ten set to play.
explanation.walkthrough: DJs here are dinner jackets, not disc jockeys; 'in' and 'with' just gather the O and X into the pool for 'to change'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinner jacket is the formal evening coat Americans call by the name of a New York country club.

clue.text: Maybe salsa dancing in Samoa creates addiction

parts.note: salsa is an example of a dip, hence maybe

indicators.note: dancing suggests the letters of in Samoa jiggle into a new order

explanation.surface: Salsa dancing on a Pacific island becomes a habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe salsa' points to the dance, but it is the tomato sauce served as a dip.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the craving for alcohol, a specific compulsive dependency on drink.

clue.text: Revive electronic R&B covers, also on the rise

indicators.note: covers means R and B wrap around the following letter

parts.note: the letters R and B from the music genre
E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

indicators.note: on the rise in a down clue means the word is read upwards

parts.note: too means also

explanation.surface: An electronic act covers rhythm-and-blues songs, and their popularity grows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers' looks like cover versions of songs but means the letters go round E. 'on the rise' reverses TOO.
explanation.definitionFit: Restarting a computer brings it back to life, and figuratively relaunching a film franchise revives it.

clue.text: Be master of hot early swing

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, on taps
old means of an early time
to sway is to swing from side to side

explanation.surface: A musician has mastered early swing music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swing' is the jazz style on the surface, but here it is the verb to rock to and fro.
explanation.definitionFit: To rule or have dominant influence over something is to be in command of it.

clue.text: Jazz tune is up for associates

indicators.note: to jazz something up is to liven it, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A jazz tune is coming up for some colleagues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jazz ... up' together signal the anagram of TUNE and IS.
explanation.definitionFit: To associate things is to join or link them together, a verb sense of combine.

clue.text: Music genre heard racing across the Atlantic

indicators.note: heard says the genre's name is said aloud to give a word sounding the same

parts.note: indie is a genre of independent alternative rock

explanation.surface: A style of music is heard in the US motor-racing scene.
explanation.walkthrough: IndyCar is American open-wheel motor racing, named after the Indianapolis 500.
explanation.definitionFit: The short name for American single-seater motorsport, centred on Indianapolis, as seen from Britain.

clue.text: Blues or pop singer catches finale from The Jam

indicators.note: catches means the singer's name holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: Celine Dion is a Canadian pop singer

indicators.note: finale from means take the last letter of the word The

parts.note: to jam is to press or squeeze

explanation.surface: A blues fan asks whether a pop star covers the closing number by The Jam.
explanation.walkthrough: The Jam were a British punk-mod band; here 'Jam' is just the verb to press.
explanation.definitionFit: The blues is a low, melancholy mood, so a fit of the blues is a period of gloom.

clue.text: Stride number about crush

parts.note: a stride is a step

indicators.note: about means the abbreviation is turned around

explanation.surface: A dancer strides through a number about having a crush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crush' looks like an infatuation, but it is the verb to squash.
explanation.definitionFit: To tread on something with your foot squashes it flat, a phrasal verb for squashing.

clue.text: Elegiac classical artist fitting clothing the wrong way

parts.note: proper means fitting or appropriate

indicators.note: the wrong way means the word for the outfit is reversed

parts.note: a suit is an item of clothing

explanation.surface: A classical musician wears an outfit put on back to front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'artist' suggests a performer, but it is a Roman poet famous for his elegies.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman poet of the Augustan age, known for his love elegies to Cynthia, counts as a classical artist.

clue.text: Single backing track about German with sin

indicators.note: backing means the word is written backwards

parts.note: single means one

indicators.note: about means the railway letters go round the German word

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway, a track
mit is the German word for with

explanation.surface: A single's backing track features a German singer, and that's sinful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing track' reads as a recording term, but 'backing' reverses ONE and 'track' is RY.
explanation.definitionFit: A great wickedness or outrageous moral wrong, the older sense of the word, fits a sin.

clue.text: Funk from a person by boisterous area of town

parts.note: funk can mean a strong smell, and BO is body odour
rough means boisterous, as in rough play

explanation.surface: Funk music played by a rowdy local.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funk' is a music genre on the surface but here is an old word for a stink.
explanation.definitionFit: A town district with its own council or a parliamentary constituency is a municipal division.

clue.text: Member of girl group on track as support for Stevie Wonder?

parts.note: a Guide is a member of the Girl Guides
to dog someone is to track them

explanation.surface: A girl-group singer on a track backing Stevie Wonder.
explanation.walkthrough: Stevie Wonder is blind, so the question mark marks a playful example of help for a blind person.
explanation.definitionFit: A trained animal leading a blind person is a form of aid for the sightless, like the singer.

clue.text: Rag time ally abroad welcomes, giving a wave

indicators.note: welcomes means the letters take another word inside them

parts.note: ami is French for friend, an ally abroad
a rag is a tabloid newspaper, such as The Sun

explanation.surface: A friend from abroad greets the ragtime music with a wave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rag time' looks like ragtime music; it is two pieces, the paper and T.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge sea surge caused by an earthquake is a giant tidal swell.

clue.text: Look up engaging American metal performances

indicators.note: engaging means the reversed word holds the following letters
up in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: to seem is to look, as in 'look tired'
tin is a metal

explanation.surface: Fans look up an American heavy-metal band's gigs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'metal' suggests the music genre, but it is the element tin.
explanation.definitionFit: Afternoon shows at a theatre or cinema are daytime showings.

clue.text: Folk star's alarming words

parts.note: men are folk, people
an ace is a star performer

explanation.surface: A folk singer's lyrics are alarming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Folk' is the music genre on the surface; here it simply means people.
explanation.definitionFit: Threats are spoken intimidations, alarming statements of intent to harm.

clue.text: Rocking A-side he includes very tacky

indicators.note: includes means the rearranged letters hold the next one inside
rocking means the letters are shaken up into a new order

explanation.surface: He puts a rock song on the A-side, which is very naff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tacky' looks like a judgement on taste but means sticky.
explanation.definitionFit: Glue and similar sticky substances are tacky to the touch.

clue.text: Thrash from French heavy metal artist's empty

parts.note: de is French for from
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron, a heavy metal

indicators.note: empty means the inside of the word artist is removed, keeping its ends

explanation.surface: A French heavy-metal artist's thrash album is hollow.
explanation.walkthrough: Thrash is a heavy-metal genre on the surface; here it means to beat soundly.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrash an opponent is to beat them heavily, a synonym for overcoming.

clue.text: Charm of baroque tuba: euphony in extremis!

indicators.note: baroque means ornate or bizarre, so the letters are twisted
in extremis takes the extreme letters, first and last, of euphony

explanation.surface: The appeal of a baroque tuba lies in its sweet sound at the climax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'baroque' passes for a musical period but is the anagram signal on TUBA plus E and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Charm is attractiveness or loveliness, the quality of being pleasing to look at.

clue.text: Hot Egyptian soul piece

parts.note: the ba was one part of the soul in ancient Egyptian belief
the king is a chess piece

explanation.surface: A hot soul track from Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soul' suggests the music, but the ba is an ancient Egyptian notion of the spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, a very hot day is described as scorching, like an oven.

clue.text: Love loud tango — what about gospel's wrong?

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O
ff, fortissimo, means very loud in music
T is tango in the radio alphabet

indicators.note: about means the word is turned round

parts.note: eh is a way of saying what?
Mark is one of the four Gospels

explanation.surface: A love song with a loud tango: what about gospel music being wrong?
explanation.walkthrough: 'gospel' suggests the music style but is the Gospel of St Mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Being inaccurate or mistaken is like missing the target, so the idiom means incorrect.

clue.text: Kelvin and Duke, say, pirouetting to bop

indicators.note: pirouetting means spinning round, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: K is the symbol for kelvin, the unit of temperature
a nob is an aristocrat, a duke for example

explanation.surface: Two men, Kelvin and the Duke, twirl as they dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bop' looks like a dance but is a light blow.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for a knock or hit on the head.

clue.text: Pop group from 3 bringing down a cake

indicators.note: bringing down in a down clue means one letter is moved lower in the word

parts.note: ABBA is the pop group from the country at 3-down

explanation.surface: A pop group brings down a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: In the down entry, moving the first A down one place turns the band's name into the sponge.
explanation.definitionFit: A rum-soaked yeast sponge is a type of dessert pastry, the rum version being well known.

clue.text: Singer's feature in garage thus captivates you

indicators.note: captivates means the letters capture the next one inside

parts.note: a car is found in a garage
so means thus
U is text-speak for you

explanation.surface: A singer's car in the garage charms you.
explanation.walkthrough: Enrico Caruso was a famous Italian operatic tenor; the 's is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An early twentieth-century Neapolitan tenor, among the most famous operatic vocalists ever recorded.

clue.text: Did dub blend, one in an innovative style

indicators.note: in an innovative style means the letters are rearranged in a new way

explanation.surface: A producer made a dub mix, blending one track innovatively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dub' looks like the reggae remix style, but it means to make someone a knight.
explanation.definitionFit: To dub someone is to tap their shoulder with a sword, raising them to the nobility.
